Let me work through the key passages:

1. The Haley character description — the draft compresses it but retains key elements (ring-laden, seals, Murray's Grammar). The narrative irony of "did not seem, strictly speaking, to come under the species" is preserved in shortened form.

2. Shelby's soliloquy — "Is thy servant a dog, that he should do this thing?" — present verbatim. Good.

3. Haley's "second Wilberforce" moment — present.

4. The narrator's direct address: "Perhaps you laugh too, dear reader; but you know humanity comes out in a variety of strange forms now-a-days" — present, verbatim essentially.

5. "Humanity, sir, I may say, is the great pillar of my management" — present.

6. The shadow of law passage — "over and above the scene there broods a portentous shadow—the shadow of _law_" — the draft has "over all broods a portentous shadow—the shadow of law" — slightly flattened ("over and above the scene" → "over all") but recognizable.

7. "so long as the failure, or misfortune, or imprudence, or death" — draft drops "misfortune" from the list, minor.

8. Mrs. Shelby description — the draft retains the key passage about husband expecting to get into heaven through her superabundance.

9. The Eliza scene with mistress — substantially preserved.

10. Key missing item: Haley's speech about "Well, I've got just as much conscience as any man in business can afford to keep,—just a little, you know, to swear by, as 't were" — present in draft. Good.

11. The narrator digression on Tom Loker — the draft omits a key characterization: "for a better hearted feller never broke bread; 't was his _system_, sir." This is a voice-distinctive ironic moment, but relatively minor.

12. Missing: Haley's self-praise passage is somewhat compressed — the specific "if I have once, I reckon I have a hundred times" and "they have paid their passage" joke is absent from the draft. This is voice-establishing Haley dialogue.

13. The "out of sight, out of mind" formulation — present.

14. Mrs. Shelby: "to that natural magnanimity and generosity of mind which one often marks as characteristic of the women of Kentucky" — draft has "to the magnanimity common to Kentucky women" — flattened but recognizable.

15. The draft drops the brief scene where Mr. Shelby and Haley "silently picked their nuts" before the final negotiation — minor but characterful.

16. Haley's monologue about Tom Loker omits: "only the very devil with niggers,—on principle 't was, you see, for a better hearted feller never broke bread; 't was his _system_, sir." This ironic juxtaposition (cruel on principle yet good-hearted) is interpretively important and voice-distinctive.

17. The draft also drops Haley's self-assessment: "I've been told so; if I have once, I reckon I have a hundred times" and "they have paid their passage, I may say" — this joke is character-establishing.

18. The mildest form of slavery paragraph — the source has "not requiring those periodic seasons of hurry and pressure that are called for in the business of more southern districts" vs draft "not calling for those periodic hurries of more southern districts" — slightly flattened.

None of these seem high severity (no verbatim-tagged signatures are missing entirely). Let me assess medium severity items:

- The Tom Loker ironic characterization ("for a better hearted ffellow never broke bread; 't was his _system_, sir") is a voice-distinctive ironic passage — its absence flattens the satire. Medium.
- "they have paid their passage" joke — present in source as a laugh moment, absent in draft. Low-medium.
- The "silently picked their nuts" interlude — minor, low.
